purpose: Test a broader ordinary-determinant diagonal-extraction model than v1.1. The target P0 coefficient is a sum of principal minors over clause transversals. A determinant sandwich det(A K B) produces all rectangular minors K[S,T]. Prove that any K-independent linear combination of such sandwiches that projects exactly onto S=T for every generic K needs at least one term per transversal.

setup.ground: q occurrence ports partitioned into m nonempty clause blocks C_1,...,C_m.
setup.transversals: T={S subseteq [q]: |S intersect C_i|=1 for every i}; N=|T|=product_i |C_i|.
setup.generic_target: Q_T(K)=sum_{S in T} det K[S,S] for an arbitrary symbolic q by q matrix K.
setup.allowed_term: For j=1,...,r choose K-independent matrices A_j of size m by q and B_j of size q by m and scalar gamma_j, and use gamma_j det(A_j K B_j).

theorem.name: ORDINARY_CAUCHY_BINET_DIAGONAL_PROJECTOR_NEEDS_TRANSVERSAL_RANK
theorem.statement: If sum_{j=1}^r gamma_j det(A_j K B_j)=Q_T(K) identically for every q by q matrix K over a field, then r>=N=|T|.
proof: Apply Cauchy-Binet twice. Each j-th term expands as sum_{|S|=|U|=m} alpha_j(S) beta_j(U) det K[S,U], where alpha_j(S)=gamma_j det A_j[:,S] and beta_j(U)=det B_j[U,:].

For a generic symbolic matrix K, its m by m minors det K[S,U] are linearly independent as polynomials across distinct row/column set pairs (S,U): every monomial in such a minor uses exactly row set S and column set U, so no nonzero linear combination can cancel between different pairs.
Therefore equality with Q_T forces the coefficient kernel W(S,U)=sum_j alpha_j(S) beta_j(U) to equal 1 when S=U belongs to T and 0 on all other pairs.
Restrict W to the N by N rows/columns indexed by T. The target restriction is exactly the identity matrix I_N.
Each j contributes one outer product alpha_j|_T times beta_j|_T, hence has matrix rank at most one. A sum of r such terms has rank at most r.
theorem.exponential_corollary: If all m clause blocks have three occurrences, N=3^m. Thus no polynomial number of ordinary K-independent determinant sandwiches can implement generic principal-transversal diagonal extraction.

scoped_finite_controls.naive_sandwich: Taking one clause-incidence selector A and det(A K A^T) mixes S!=T rectangular minors rather than selecting only principal terms.
source_examples: On the frozen bounded-occurrence UNSAT five-clause control, the exact P0 target W is 0 while det(A K A^T) is nonzero.
There are SAT bounded-occurrence controls with W>0 while det(A K A^T)=0.

ruled_out: A polynomial-size K-independent linear combination of ordinary determinant sandwiches claimed to be a universal diagonal projector for arbitrary K.
The naive one-sandwich replacement Q_T(K)=det(A K A^T).
not_ruled_out: Algorithms exploiting the special block-diagonal K2/K3 source family rather than working for arbitrary K.
Nonlinear/adaptive formula-dependent transforms in which the selector depends on K in a nontrivial way.
Pfaffian/exterior contractions not expressible as a polynomial linear combination of ordinary sandwiches.
A source-specific rank-3 claw augmentation theorem.

next_target.name: E8_SOURCE_SPECIFIC_K3_DIAGONAL_CONTRACTION_V3_6
next_target.directive: Generic equality projection is exponentially ranked, so stop searching for a universal K-independent diagonal projector. Exploit the actual source K: a direct sum of fixed K2/K3/identity blocks with 0/1 principal minors, together with rank<=3 clause projectors. Seek a polynomial contraction that uses these local algebraic identities before diagonal extraction, or a combinatorially equivalent global claw augmentation.
